reason: Selected same-model/game memory comparison shows summaries can help reusable strategy but lose necessary state details.

candidates.title: Compare distilled rules with retained state-rich history
candidates.rule: When turning agent experience into memory, compare compact summaries with direct interaction history on the actual task; retain detailed evidence where decisions depend on exact local state.
candidates.passage: Summary Memory is therefore a selective improvement mechanism
candidates.location: Section 6 memory comparison, Table 7 and trajectory cases
candidates.finding: Across seven model pairs per game, summaries improve average scores on Tetris, Trust and Nullify but lose on Minesweeper, PvZ and Snake. Individual models can reverse a game-level trend. The task-structure explanation comes from qualitative trace analysis.
models: Seven-model panel; inspected cases include GPT-5.5, GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, o3-mini and Gemini Flash variants
candidates.conditions: Same model-game pairs compare history organization after exploration, followed by strict executable evaluation.
candidates.limitations: The study compares memory modes, not a validated adaptive selector. Strategic-rule versus state-detail classification is interpretive. Game-specific learned policies should not be transferred to unrelated user interactions.
candidates.validation_test: Compare raw history, summaries and summaries with retrievable original states on new episodes; measure execution success, omitted state information, token use and model-specific reversals.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
